hero.headline: Port St. Lucie's 6,000-seat soccer stadium groundbreaking set for November, new renderings unveiled
hero.body:
Professional soccer is still set to begin next year in Port St. Lucie, and the club this week released new renderings of its 6,000-seat stadium. The stadium will be built at the Walton & One development, a 46-acre mixed-use redevelopment project located along U.S. 1 and Walton Road. Representatives for Port St. Lucie SC announced Friday that groundbreaking is anticipated later this year, with current plans targeting November. While the club's inaugural season begins in 2027, the future stadium is scheduled to open in early 2028. The team has not announced where they plan to play next year while the facility is under construction. The club posted Thursday on social media that their home venue will be a place where soccer, community, and unforgettable moments will come together. The team said on X that every space has been designed to create unforgettable experiences, and from matchdays to concerts, festivals, and community events, this is a destination built for everyone.

Barber Focus Sanders at Sapp's Barbershop said the stadium offers more business because it's going to bring more people over here, including people coming from maybe out of town who didn't get a haircut. Port St. Lucie resident Zach Woods said you can't really even get out here on US-1 before this, calling it a nightmare, so he thinks the additional traffic on gamedays will be huge. Sanders said he is not liking the traffic that's going to come, but he is liking the business traffic. Woods said he thinks there's nothing to do in PSL for the most part and this may be the first cool thing that we've ever actually brought here. The team said this week that ticket deposits are currently available online. It was announced last October that the city had been awarded a United Soccer League League One Team. Port St. Lucie city council members unanimously approved both the funding and operating agreements. The city said the stadium is an $80 million economic investment, and no taxpayer money will be used for its construction.

cards.headline: Woman accused of using vehicle in three-person assault in St. Lucie County
cards.teaser: Tioniea Hines, 22, is being held in St. Lucie County Jail on $75,000 bond. She faces three counts of aggravated battery with a deadly weapon.
cards.body:
Tioniea Hines, 22, is in St. Lucie County Jail on $75,000 bond and faces three counts of aggravated battery with a deadly weapon. The charges stem from an alleged assault involving three people.

Authorities accused Hines of using a vehicle in the assault. The incident occurred in St. Lucie County.

Hines remains in custody at the St. Lucie County Jail. Bond has been set at $75,000.

cards.headline: Immigration enforcement shifts to traffic stops across South Florida as detention numbers rise
cards.body:
South Florida immigration attorneys are reporting a significant shift in how federal and local law enforcement are conducting immigration arrests, moving away from high-profile raids toward more targeted detentions during routine traffic stops. The change appears to coincide with Markwayne Mullin replacing Kristi Noem as Homeland Security Secretary in March.

Renata Castro, an immigration attorney based in Coral Springs, said her office has seen a marked increase in detained cases coming across her desk. Castro said the uptick is driven largely by traffic-related detentions that result in immigration holds. She contrasted the current approach with methods used during Noem's tenure, describing those earlier operations as involving arrests without warrants and creating what she called a big spectacle overall. Immigration attorneys previously questioned the legality of many detentions carried out during that period.

Castro said she does not have the same legal concerns about the current approach, noting that while arrests are still happening without warrants, they are following safeguards that local law enforcement must abide by under the law. According to NBC News, ICE arrested 10,000 people over five days this month. Data kept by the Florida Department of Law Enforcement shows 24 immigration arrests were conducted in Martin County on Tuesday. The Martin County Sheriff's Office confirmed FDLE was the agency behind those arrests.

The shift in enforcement strategy marks a tactical change in how immigration law is being carried out across South Florida. Castro said the current approach is resulting in higher detention numbers while adhering to existing legal frameworks that govern how local law enforcement conducts arrests. FDLE and ICE have not yet responded to requests for comment on the new enforcement patterns.

cards.headline: Florida back-to-school sales tax holiday runs July 20 through August 20
cards.teaser: Florida families can save hundreds of dollars during the state's 32-day tax-free shopping period for school supplies, clothing, computers and educational items.
cards.body:
Florida's annual back-to-school sales tax holiday runs from July 20 through Aug. 20, 2026, offering 32 days of tax-free shopping on essential items for the new school year. The exemption covers clothing items under $100, school supplies under $50, learning aids and puzzles under $30, and computers and accessories under $1,500 per item.

Qualifying items include shirts, pants, shoes, backpacks, notebooks, pens, markers, lunch boxes, educational toys, laptops, tablets, electronic book readers, keyboards, printers and educational software. The tax exemption does not apply at theme parks, entertainment complexes, hotels or airports. Items ordered online during the holiday period qualify for the exemption even if delivered after Aug. 20.

Florida retailers have no option to opt out of the sales tax holiday. All qualifying purchases must be processed tax-free during the designated period. A family spending $500 on qualifying items could save $35 in sales tax.

cards.headline: St. Lucie Mets Snap Three-Game Skid With 4-1 Win Over Jupiter
cards.teaser:
The St. Lucie Mets snapped a three-game losing streak Saturday evening with a wire-to-wire 4-1 win over the Jupiter Hammerheads at Roger Dean Chevrolet Stadium.

St. Lucie needed o
cards.body:
The St. Lucie Mets snapped a three-game losing streak Saturday evening with a wire-to-wire 4-1 win over the Jupiter Hammerheads at Roger Dean Chevrolet Stadium.

St. Lucie needed only minutes to take control. The first three batters of the game all reached and scored before an out was recorded. Elian Peña opened with a single, Mike Tauchman doubled him home, and Trey Snyder followed with a two-run homer off Walin Castillo for a 3-0 lead.

Julio Zayas added a solo shot with two outs in the third to push the margin to 4-0.

That was more than enough for starter Emilio Obispo, who threw five shutout innings and lowered his season ERA to 1.82. He scattered four singles, walked three and struck out six to earn his fourth win of the year.

Obispo worked out of trouble when it mattered. He struck out Josh Hogue to strand the bases loaded in the third, induced a double play to end the fourth, and retired the side in order in the fifth to finish his outing.

Jupiter loaded the bases against Calvin Ziegler in the sixth. Ziegler struck out Jake McCutheon for the second out before Zack Mack entered and ended the threat with a popout. Mack went 2.1 innings and allowed one unearned run, which came in the eighth when Andres Valor stole third and scored on a throwing error.

Elwis Mijares closed it out with a 1-2-3 ninth on 11 pitches for his second save.

Tauchman, rehabbing a torn meniscus, went 1 for 3 with the double, an RBI and a run while playing six innings in left field in his first rehab game with St. Lucie. Snyder led the offense at 2 for 4 with the homer and two RBI.

The Mets (5-13, 38-46) and Hammerheads (8-12, 45-41) close their six-game series Sunday at Roger Dean Chevrolet Stadium. A win would give St. Lucie its first 3-3 series split of 2026. First pitch is 12:30 p.m.

cards.headline: Florida home insurance market improves as insurers return and rates decline
cards.teaser: Florida's home insurance market is showing signs of improvement with more insurers returning to the state and some rates declining.
cards.body: Florida's home insurance market shows signs of improvement as more insurers return and some rates decline. The changes represent a shift in the state's troubled property insurance landscape, which has faced years of challenges including company insolvencies and rate increases.

cards.headline: Port St. Lucie teen surprised with FIFA World Cup finals trip after being named Southeast Region Youth of the Year
cards.body:
A Port St. Lucie teenager named Youth of the Year for the Southeast Region of the Boys & Girls Clubs of America is heading to the FIFA World Cup finals after receiving a surprise announcement at the Boys & Girls Club of St. Lucie County in Fort Pierce. Enrique Rosario Liz will serve as one of 12 club members from across the country selected to be an official Coca-Cola flag bearer at the FIFA World Cup finals on July 19. The surprise came courtesy of the Boys & Girls Clubs of America and their partnership with the Coca-Cola Company.

Rosario Liz had already been juggling a packed summer, preparing for move-in at the University of Florida and an internship, but said the World Cup had been on his mind. "My time is really being taken up by the World Cup right now, forcing my parents to watch every game," Rosario Liz said. When the box containing the news was walked into the room surrounded by fellow club members, his reaction was immediate. "This is crazy. I mean, this is so insane," Rosario Liz said. Along with the trip, he also received official gear inside the box. Rosario Liz credited the club with shaping who he has become as a leader. "The club really helped me to find what my leadership style was going to be, and really redefined what my definition of leadership was," Rosario Liz said.

cards.headline: Jupiter Inlet Lighthouse offers 165 years of history with breathtaking views
cards.teaser: Built in 1860, the Jupiter Inlet Lighthouse has guided countless ships along Florida's Atlantic coast for more than 165 years.
cards.body:
Standing at the base of the Jupiter Inlet Lighthouse, the striking red brick tower rises high above the inlet. Built in 1860, the lighthouse has guided countless ships along Florida's Atlantic coast for more than 165 years. The 105-step climb to the top was well worth every step. Reaching the gallery, visitors are rewarded with breathtaking panoramic views. The Atlantic Ocean stretched endlessly to the east, while the turquoise waters of the Jupiter Inlet met the Loxahatchee and Indian rivers below. Boats glided through the channel, and the sea breeze made the warm Florida morning feel perfect.

After the climb, visitors can explore the museum grounds. Walking among the restored historic buildings, visitors learn about the lighthouse's fascinating past, from its construction before the Civil War to its years as an active Coast Guard station. The powerful Fresnel lens has been shining for mariners for more than a century and a half.
